rationale: Baseline. Dual-domain U-Net (c=16) on Wagner @ 128 sparse views, AdamW lr=3e-4 wd=1e-4, 8 epochs, 400 synthetic ellipse phantoms. Converged at loss 0.00037. PSNR 31.86 dB SSIM 0.6445, headroom 0.5680 over the sparse-view FBP baseline (PSNR 24.57).

Tried horizontal-flip data augmentation (effective 2x dataset) with epochs halved 8->4 to keep total step count constant. Val 0.6445 -> 0.6418 (-0.4%), within noise. Augmentation at fixed compute did not help on this 400-phantom random-ellipse subset. Reverting solver.py to iter-1 baseline.

Increased unet_c=16 -> 24 (params 0.466M -> 1.045M, 2.25x). Val SSIM 0.6445 -> 0.6343 (-1.6%), just over noise. Bigger model overfits the 400-phantom subset slightly. c=16 confirmed near optimal at this data budget. Reverting.

Lowered AdamW lr 3e-4 -> 1e-4. Val SSIM 0.6445 -> 0.6486 (+0.4%), PSNR 31.86 -> 31.95 (+0.09 dB). Marginal but consistent improvement at fixed compute. Training loss plateau (0.00037) reached at same epoch in both — the gain is from a slightly better minimum, not under-training.

Added cosine LR schedule (1e-4 -> 1e-6) on top of iter-4's flat lr=1e-4. Val SSIM 0.6486 -> 0.6490 (+0.06%), within noise. Training loss plateau (~0.00038) reached at same epoch as the flat-LR run. Convergence is not LR-schedule-limited at this configuration.

Swapped Noise2Inverse loss MSE -> L1 (added n2i_step in solver.py since DualDomainPipeline.training_step is fixed). SSIM 0.6486 -> 0.6509 (+0.4% in-noise), but RMSE-based headroom 0.5727 -> 0.5664 (-1.1%, outside noise). Classic MSE/L1 trade-off: L1 sharper, MSE more pixel-accurate. Pentathlon scores headroom -> discard.

Increased train_n 400->600. SSIM 0.6486 -> 0.6471 (-0.2% noise), headroom 0.5727 -> 0.5755 (+0.5% within noise). Marginal positive on headroom but training time +50% (5:00). We are saturated on the synthetic random-ellipse distribution at c=16.

Asymmetric: proj_denoiser c=24, image_denoiser c=16 (total 0.76M params). Hypothesis was that proj-domain (1152x736 canvas, complex streak structure) benefits from more capacity. Val 0.6486 -> 0.6421 (-1.0%), headroom 0.5727 -> 0.5661 (-1.1%). Both directions of capacity change from symmetric c=16/c=16 hurt. The symmetric configuration is robust.

SmallUNet residual=True -> False (predict image directly instead of noise residual). Val 0.6486 -> 0.6371 (-1.8%), headroom 0.5727 -> 0.5562 (-2.9%). The noise-prediction (residual) parameterization is materially better here.

unet_c=16 -> 12 (params 0.47M -> 0.26M, Occam test). Val 0.6486 -> 0.6413 (-1.1%), headroom 0.5727 -> 0.5652 (-1.3%). c=12 also loses, just as c=24 lost in iter-3. The optimum is now bracketed at c=16 from both sides.

Adam vs AdamW with weight_decay=1e-4. Val 0.6486 -> 0.6452 (-0.5%), headroom 0.5727 -> 0.5707 (-0.4%) — both within noise. wd=1e-4 makes essentially no difference at this configuration; AdamW marginally preferred.

Added forward-projection data-consistency MSE(R*y_hat, x_a) at lambda=0.05. Val SSIM 0.6486 -> 0.4745 (-26.8%), headroom 0.5727 -> 0.5110 (-10.8%). Catastrophic: the consistency term against the *noisy* input sinogram pulls the model toward fitting noise, defeating the denoising objective.

Halved consistency_weight further from 0.05 -> 0.005. Val 0.6486 -> 0.5102 (-21.4%), still catastrophic. Even tiny lambda > 0 pulls the model toward fitting noisy sino. The MSE(R*y_hat, x_noisy) consistency term is structurally incompatible with self-supervised denoising — there is no positive lambda regime.

TwoStageDenoiser per domain (stack 2 SmallUNets, 0.93M params, doubles depth). Val 0.6486 -> 0.6424 (-1.0%), headroom 0.5727 -> 0.5660 (-1.2%). Train_time 326s (over 5-min budget). Same overfit pattern as iter-3 c=24 (1.05M params): at 400 phantoms, ~1M params is the overfit threshold whether you spend it on width or depth.

Lowered lr 1e-4 -> 5e-5. Val 0.6486 -> 0.6451 (-0.5%), headroom 0.5727 -> 0.5701 (-0.5%) — both within noise. Loss plateau at 0.00038 (one tick worse than 0.00037 at lr=1e-4). LR=1e-4 confirmed as the local optimum: 3e-4 below, 5e-5 below, 1e-4 best.

Replaced image_denoiser = SmallUNet with UNetPlusBF = SmallUNet + TrainableBilateralFilter2d tail (Wagner 2022). Val SSIM 0.6486 -> 0.6537 (+0.8%), headroom 0.5727 -> 0.5760 (+0.6%) — first improvement since iter-4. BF adds ~3 params, train_time +17%. The interpretable edge-preserving filter sharpens the U-Net's output on sparse-view streaks.

Extended BF tail to proj_denoiser too (symmetric Wagner-2022 dual BF). Val 0.6537 -> 0.6510 (-0.4%), headroom 0.5760 -> 0.5738 (-0.4%). Sinograms lack the anatomical edges BF exploits; asymmetric (BF on image only) is the winner. Building on iter-16, not iter-17.

bf_kernel 7 -> 11. Training succeeded (loss 0.00037, normal), but pipe.predict(val_noisy) at val_n=100 OOMed: BF unfold creates 121x channels for a 512^2 image, ~12 GB intermediate. Need either smaller kernel or chunked validation.
bf_kernel 7 -> 9. Val 0.6537 -> 0.6499 (-0.6%), headroom 0.5760 -> 0.5739 (-0.4%). 7 is the BF window sweet spot: 7 > 9 > 11 (OOM).
epochs 8 -> 10 on iter-16 baseline. Val 0.6537 -> 0.6496 (-0.6%), headroom 0.5760 -> 0.5738 (-0.4%). Loss plateau 0.00037 hit by epoch 6 in both 8 and 10 epoch runs; extra epochs don't help.
Stacked 2 BFs after the U-Net (n_bf=2). Val 0.6537 -> 0.6478 (-0.9%), headroom 0.5760 -> 0.5727 (-0.6%). Two BFs in series over-smooth — kernel=7 once is enough.

weight_decay 1e-4 -> 1e-3 on iter-16 baseline. Val 0.6537 -> 0.6518 (-0.3%), headroom 0.5760 -> 0.5748 (-0.2%) — both within noise. Stronger WD doesn't compound with BF; the small wd was already adequate.

Re-measurement of iter-16 c=16+BF architecture under FIXED calibration (data_range=display_max-display_min=0.05). Headroom 0.576 unchanged (RMSE-ratio is scale-invariant); val_ssim 0.6537->0.3070 because auto data_range was previously inflated by FBP overshoot (~0.07). All future iterations compete against THIS calibrated baseline. Also adds GPU pin q8000 + chunked validation so iter does not OOM on smaller cards.

Cross-ported spawn-agent B (dl-sparse-view-res) iter-2 winner: symmetric 6-block c=32 GroupNorm-ReLU residual stack with global residual head, replacing the U-Net+BF (iter-16/24 baseline). Result under calibration: val_ssim 0.3070->0.3099 (+0.9%), headroom 0.5759->0.5807 (+0.83%, NEW BEST) at 0.225 M params vs 0.466 M (half the parameter count). Confirms Sidky 2022 finding that residual / DnCNN-style families are competitive with U-Net on sparse-view CT. Single change: build_denoisers now returns ResidualStack pair when img_denoiser="resnet"; everything else (lr, epochs, wd, seed, calibration) held constant.

Per-epoch noise resampling (new (phantom, low-dose-noise) pair every epoch, same 400 phantoms; effective 3200 train pairs). Headroom 0.5807 -> 0.5768 (-0.67%), val_ssim 0.3099 -> 0.2947 (-4.9%). Worse. Hypothesis: the dual-domain N2I training_step already does its own per-batch noise split (Wagner 2022 Noise2Inverse), so adding per-epoch noise variation breaks that internal noise structure rather than augmenting it. Discard; reverting solver to iter-25 baseline.

iter-27 attempt: cross-port spawn agent B iter-14 winner (residual-in-residual with learnable per-block alpha, init=0.1, EDSR/ReZero spirit; 12 extra scalar params). Submitted as Slurm 760465 on lme171 -> NVML driver/library version mismatch (Slurm exit 18 = node failure). Pure infra fail, not a solver bug. Adding lme171 to the sbatch --exclude list and resubmitting under the same iter#.

iter-28 (resubmit of crashed iter-27 attempt after fixing sbatch bad-node exclusion): cross-ported spawn-agent-B iter-14 winner — residual-in-residual with learnable per-block alpha scaling (init=0.1, EDSR Lim+2017 + ReZero Bachlechner+2020). 12 extra scalar params total (6 blocks x 2 nets). Headroom 0.5807 (iter-25) -> 0.5833 (+0.26pp, NEW MAIN BEST). val_rmse 0.005537 -> 0.005503 (-0.6%). Effectively ties spawn-B iter-14 leader (0.587) within FP noise. Confirms the learnable-alpha scaling generalises from B/res slot to main/iter-25 baseline.

iter-29: bumped res_scale_init 0.1 -> 0.3 on iter-28 baseline. Headroom 0.5833 -> 0.5735 (-0.98pp), val_rmse 0.005503 -> 0.005632 (+2.3%). Aggressive alpha-init overshoots; alongside spawn B iter-15 (alpha=0.05, -4.9%) this brackets the basin: 0.05 < 0.1 < 0.3 with 0.1 the sweet spot. Discard, revert.

iter-30: lr 1e-4 -> 5e-5 on iter-28 alpha-scaling baseline. Headroom 0.5833 -> 0.5636 (-1.97pp), val_rmse +4.7%. Too slow — at 8 epochs the lower lr underfits; the network has not had time to grow alpha and exit near-identity. Discard, revert.

iter-31: CosineAnnealingLR(T_max=epochs=8, eta_min=0) over the iter-28 alpha-scaling baseline. Headroom 0.5833 -> 0.5700 (-1.33pp), val_rmse +3.2%. Annealing to 0 over 8 epochs starves the late epochs (last 2 train at lr<2e-5) — same underfitting failure mode as iter-30 lr=5e-5, just delayed. Discard, revert.

iter-32: weight_decay 1e-4 -> 0 on the iter-28 alpha-scaling residual-in-residual baseline. Headroom 0.5833 -> 0.5906 (+0.73pp, FIRST TIME ANY AGENT EXCEEDS 0.59). val_rmse 0.005503 -> 0.005407 (-1.7%). Hypothesis confirmed: AdamW WD was decaying the learnable per-block alpha scalars (init 0.1), pulling them back toward 0 and preventing them from growing into their useful range. WD=0 lets alpha discover its right magnitude. This compounds with iter-28 to give the new team-wide best. NEW OVERALL BEST (was spawn-B iter-14 at hr=0.587).

iter-33: epochs 8 -> 10 on the iter-32 (wd=0) baseline. Headroom 0.5906 -> 0.5699 (-2.07pp), val_rmse +5.0%. Strong overfit signal. Same outcome as spawn-B iter-20 (epochs=10 at wd=1e-4) which also discarded with -2.3pp. Independent of weight decay: the 8-epoch / 400-phantom budget is data-bound — more epochs overfits the small training set. The wd=0 finding from iter-32 does NOT compose with extending training; epochs=8 is the right operating point at train_n=400. Discard, revert to iter-32 keep.

iter-34: batch_size 1 -> 2 on iter-32 (wd=0) baseline. Headroom 0.5906 -> 0.5634 (-2.72pp). Bigger batches reduce gradient stochasticity at the cost of halving the steps-per-epoch (200 vs 400) and effectively doubling the per-step lr. With only 400 phantoms the loss of SGD noise hurts generalisation; the halved opt steps also give the per-block alpha fewer growth opportunities. Discard, revert.

iter-35: SWA over last 2 of 8 epochs (uniform mean of epoch-end state_dicts), loaded into pipe before validation. Headroom 0.5906 -> 0.5749 (-1.57pp). Different from Agent A iter-27/29 finding: SWA gave +0.15-0.6pp on UNet+BF / NAFNet bases. On the alpha-scaling residual-in-residual + wd=0 base, SWA HURTS — likely because the per-block alpha grows late in training (epochs 6-8) and averaging across those late states dilutes the most-converged alpha. SWA is base-substrate dependent; do not assume it composes. Discard, revert.

iter-36: added Wagner BF tail to the image-domain ResidualStack on top of the iter-32 (alpha+wd=0) baseline. Cross-port attempt of Agent A iter-29 winning pattern (NAFNet + SWA + 2BF). Headroom 0.5906 -> 0.5790 (-1.16pp). Confirms Agent B iter-11 verdict at the new substrate: BF tails are U-Net specific. The residual stack at full resolution already does local edge processing; layering a BF on top oversmooths. wd=0 did NOT unlock BF composition. Discard, revert.

iter-37: ReLU -> GELU on iter-32 baseline. Headroom 0.5906 -> 0.5584 (-3.22pp). GELU smooth tail interacts badly with the alpha-scaling residual path; ReLU hard-zero kept features sparse, which composed well with the learnable alpha. Activation choice matters substantially here. Discard, revert.

iter-38: linear lr warmup over epoch 1 (1e-5 -> 1e-4) on iter-32 baseline. Headroom 0.5906 -> 0.5866 (-0.41pp). Smaller regression than other discards but still negative. Warmup steals ~1 of 8 effective training epochs (~12.5% of compute); at the data-budget ceiling (cross-confirmed by main iter-33, Agent B iter-20: epochs=10 overfits regardless of wd), every fractional epoch of useful training matters. Discard, revert.

iter-39: alpha scaling 12 scalars (per-block) -> 384 scalars (per-channel, 6 blocks × 2 nets × c=32). Headroom 0.5906 -> 0.5875 (-0.31pp). Per-channel granularity is too noisy at train_n=400; the per-block scalar acts as effective regularisation via parameter sharing. The 32× increase in scaling params (still tiny in absolute terms, +384 / 0.225M) doesnt help and slightly hurts. Discard, revert.

iter-40: kernel 3 -> 5 on iter-32 alpha+wd=0 baseline. Params 0.225M -> 0.620M (+176% conv weights from 9/9 -> 25/9 spatial). Slurm TIMEOUT at 10:02 / 10:00 wall, no result.json. Slower per-epoch at 0.620M; the 10-min wall doesnt fit kernel=5 + 6 blocks + 8 epochs. Revert.

iter-41: lr 1e-4 -> 2e-4 isolated at wd=0 + alpha-scaling. Headroom 0.5906 -> 0.5775 (-1.31pp). Overshoots; combined with iter-30 (lr=5e-5 underfits, hr=0.5636) the lr basin around 1e-4 is tight on both sides. Discard, revert.

iter-42: GroupNorm -> BatchNorm on iter-32 baseline. Headroom 0.5906 -> 0.5889 (-0.18pp, smallest discard yet). At batch_size=1 BN reduces to per-instance affine, so the change is essentially semantic — it loses the cross-channel-group normalisation but adds learnable affine. The tiny regression suggests GroupNorm is the right norm; BN is not horribly wrong but not better. Discard, revert.

iter-43: cross-port of spawn agent B iter-34 — AdamW param-group split (wd=1e-4 on 222K conv weights, wd=0 on 2.4K alpha/norm/bias). Result: 0.5906 -> 0.5851 (-0.55pp). The cross-port does NOT transfer: B improved by REMOVING wd from small params (1e-4 globally -> split); main HURTS by ADDING wd to conv params (0 globally -> split). The substrate-dependence is structural: Bs residual-stack at iter-14 had conv-overfit headroom that wd=1e-4 absorbed; mains iter-32 baseline (with the same arch + wd=0) is already past that point. wd=0 globally remains main optimal.

iter-44: epochs 8 -> 6 on iter-32 baseline. Headroom 0.5906 -> 0.5754 (-1.52pp). 6 epochs undertrain; combined with iter-33 (epochs=10 overfits -2.07pp) and Agent B iter-20 (same finding cross-substrate) the optimal epoch count is firmly 8. Symmetric basin from both sides.

iter-45: GroupNorm group target 8 -> 2 (16 channels/group, closer to LayerNorm). TIMEOUT at 10:15 / 10:00 wall. The wider-group GN has more compute cost per layer (broadcasting + reduction over more channels per group); pushed past the wall. Cannot evaluate quality.

iter-46: res_residual True -> False (predict image directly vs noise residual). Headroom 0.5906 -> 0.5709 (-1.97pp). The noise-prediction parameterisation is a strong prior — the model only needs to learn what to subtract from the FBP input, not reconstruct the image from scratch. Without it, the zero-init tail breaks (now the network must learn to output the image not zero).
